model.architecture: Looped transformer: 22 layers run twice per token (num_loops=2), unrolled at export to 44 layer executions over shared weights; reasoning model

session_defaults.notes: Reasoning model — the chat template auto-opens the <think> block and the visible answer follows </think>. Sampling is required: official recipe temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95; the model collapses under greedy decoding (do not run at temperature 0).

variants.quantization: int4 weights — blockwise (block 32) + OCTAV optimal-clipping, symmetric; embedding INT8

platform_notes: The loop makes this ~2x the per-token compute of a normal 3B — expect roughly 8B-class decode rates on CPU

CPU only. On a GPU this file emits a flood of <unk> — measured on Apple Metal and on the Galaxy S26 Adreno, with the same binary and prompt returning a correct answer on CPU. It delegates in full on both, so this is an activation-dtype numeric fault and not an op wall; use model_fp32act.litertlm for GPU.

The published card's 'GPU (Metal) 556 / 52.6 tok/s' row describes this file on that broken path. Re-measured with logs at 547.92 / 51.45 and 550.91 / 51.77 tok/s -- the numbers reproduce and mean nothing — the benchmark path never checks that any text was produced.
Not tested on an iPhone 17 Pro, so no claim is made in either direction. The sibling model_fp32act.litertlm does run there (8/8 on both backends, 2026-08-28).

measured.source: litert-lm benchmark --backend gpu --cache no -p 256 -d 256 --runs 3, two invocations: 408.65 / 409.16 tok/s prefill and 39.74 / 39.76 tok/s decode, within 0.1%; TTFT 0.6705 / 0.6710 s and engine init 3.24 / 3.31 s. The same file was separately asked to generate and returned a correct, coherent answer with the think block closed. Taken while the machine was NOT idle (load average ~3, other work running); the published card's methodology says 'otherwise idle machine', so re-take the absolute values in a quiet, serialised window before publication. The GPU:CPU ratio is the robust part -- both legs saw the same load.

same-machine CPU control, litert-lm benchmark --backend cpu --cache no -p 256 -d 256 --runs 3, one invocation; agrees with the published card's 56 / 12.5 CPU row. known_issues: Sampling is required — the model collapses under greedy decoding (official recipe: temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95)

No Galaxy S26 GPU speed row is published on purpose: each benchmark decodes ~3900 tokens because the model thinks before answering, so a pair of runs holds the GPU for over half an hour and the second is measurably throttled (prefill 46.2 then 27.0 tok/s; engine init 12.4 s then 29.2 s). Functionally it passes — full delegation, correct output, exit 0.

Some replies open with a garbled first word ('Weimplify is asked:' where 'We are asked:' belongs) and a closing </think> can appear with no opener. It is intermittent and prompt-dependent, reproduces on Mac CPU, Mac Metal and Adreno alike, is present on the Nanbeige4.1 bundle too, and is not the tokenizer — a round trip through the bundle's own SentencePiece model is clean. The answer after </think> has been correct in every case seen, so this is cosmetic rather than a correctness fault.

Runs on an iPhone 17 Pro: 8/8 on GPU (Metal) and 8/8 on CPU in an 8-question on-device sanity gate, engine init 6.77 s and 2.53 s, measured 2026-08-28. An earlier claim that it could not start there was a harness defect, not a model or device limit: the test app never created a window, so iOS killed it at the 20.00 s process-launch watchdog (0x8BADF00D) regardless of the model, which on the console is indistinguishable from an OOM kill.
